newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon signs $198 mln deal with German firm.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon signs $198 mln deal with German firm.

text.p: Lebanon signed on Thursday a $198 million deal with German firm Zublin to construct seven new faculty buildings at the new campus of state-run Lebanese University, the government's reconstruction agency said.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) said the 38-month project was part of a larger plan to bring together more Lebanese University faculties into one campus located in the area of Hadath in the southeastern part of Beirut.
The total area of faculties, research centres and a conference room to be constructed under the deal is 197,120 square metres with a capacity to handle 27,800 students.
Living accommodation for up to 2,500 students will also be built under the deal.
The agreement was signed between CDR head Nabil al-Jisr and Volker Jurowch, a member of Zublin's board of directors, in Beirut.
Work on the project will begin within three months.
At present, Lebanese University faculty buildings are scattered in east and west Beirut and other Lebanese cities.
